question_text: [NLP & LLM Engineering - Q08] How does Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) handle previously unseen out-of-vocabulary (OOV) words at inference time?

options.text: Replaces them with an unknown token [UNK]
Decomposes the novel word into known subword tokens or individual byte-level character characters
Drops the token completely from the sequence
Hashes the word to a random embedding vector

answer_explanation: BPE builds an iterative vocabulary of merged character pairs. If a complete word is missing from the vocabulary, it seamlessly falls back to composing the word from constituent subword units or UTF-8 bytes.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: BPE builds an iterative vocabulary of merged character pairs. If a complete word is missing from the vocabulary, it seamlessly falls back to composing the word from constituent subword units or UTF-8 bytes.

criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
